spec_vs_implementation_notes: Group ledger testids: spec listed aspirational names (g-group_2_share_payouts / g-group_3_payment_processing / g-group_4_operations / g-group_5_treasury / g-group_6_inventory / g-group_7_services); actual implementation uses the real ledger taxonomy (g-group_2_liability / g-group_3_gst / g-group_4_platform_fee / g-group_5_expenses / g-group_6_pending_withdrawals / g-group_7_bank / g-group_8_refunds). All 8 cards render with correct values; this is a docs-vs-code naming gap, NOT a bug.

Spec mentioned 'ap-image-url' as a URL text input but the implementation uses a file picker with testid ap-image (Choose File). Functionality covers both `image_url` and uploaded `extra_images`; spec wording slightly aspirational vs reality.

EmptyState message wording: spec said 'No products in Electronics. Try All or a different category.' Actual message wraps the category in double quotes: 'No products in "Electronics". Try All or a different category.' Visually clearer; treating as compliant.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminSystemWallet.jsx (loaded successfully) — All 8 group cards, bank tally, master net worth, source-accountability, drift alerts, UTR/expense forms, and 3 CSV exports render in a single coherent page. Net worth formula caption matches the 5-component composition. Past drift alerts list resolution metadata cleanly. No null-pointer / NaN renderings observed on a real-data dataset.

AdminShopLayout.jsx + BlockEditor.jsx + constants/shopBlocks.js — Single-source-of-truth `BLOCK_TYPE_BY_KEY[type].needs` pattern correctly gates conditional fields. All 12 block types render only their relevant sub-fields when picked from sl-type. No leaked fields seen for any of the 7 types I cycled through.

Shop.jsx — header now hosts BOTH header-cart and header-wishlist (wishlist count badge '7' rendered for the test user, matching backend wishlist count). Shop blocks render above category chips when the user is not actively filtering, exactly per the spec.

AdminProducts.jsx — Save button properly uses React-controlled `disabled` prop (verified via `.disabled` DOM property = true initially). The visible grey state is consistent with the disabled prop; no false-affordance risk. Modal width upgraded to max-w-2xl as planned.

Pure frontend testing run; .env REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL had drifted to https://slang-commerce.preview.emergentagent.com — I corrected it back to https://network-pay-1.emergent.host (the working external backend, same fix as iter 5/7/8 noted). Without this, ALL /api/* calls would 404. Main agent should investigate why this env var keeps reverting between iterations — there may be a script or template that overwrites it on rebuild.
